newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates ABN AMRO's $500 mln 5-yr bond A l-term.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates ABN AMRO's $500 mln 5-yr bond A l-term.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it assigned its A long-term debt rating to ABN AMRO's $500 million subordinated five-year bond.
"This is only the second ever issue of Tier III debt," S&P said in a statement.
"Tier III capital was introduced by the Capital Adequacy Directive (CAD) to help banks meet new capital requirements covering market risk," S&P said.

"CAD's primary objective is to provide a minimum capital framework for credit institutions and investment firms for market and other risks associated with their trading activities, to enhance the strength and stability of local and international banking systems. CAD came into effect within the European Union on January 1, 1996 but will be introduced globally after 1997," the agency said.

Valerie Hart, European editor of CreditWeek, the agency's weekly journal on credit quality, said Tier III capital was developed as a flexible instrument to partly compensate institutions for having to hold additional capital against their market risk positions.
S&P said "Tier III capital debt is attractive to investors because there is generally a lack of short-term subordinate paper in the market place."

"As a result of the minimum conditions that capital must meet to be considered Tier III, Standard & Poor's methodology is generally to rate such paper three notches (i.e., one full category) below the senior debt rating, as is the case for the ABN AMRO issue," the agency said.
"Exceptionally, the agency will rate two notches below senior debt, but only for extremely well capitalized bans with sophisticated risk management systems," Standard & Poor's said.
